title: Add to a Range, Then Count the Cells That Are at Least x

concept.title: Cut the row into blocks of about sqrt(n) cells; each block keeps a sorted copy and one lazy addition
body: Operations **add a number to every cell of a range**, and questions ask **how many cells of a range are at least `x`**. For `3 1 4 1 5` the cells at least 3 are `3, 4, 5`: 3 of them. After adding 2 to the cells 2 to 4 the row is `3 3 6 3 5`, and now all 5 are at least 3. A segment tree cannot answer "how many are at least `x`" after additions: a sum or a minimum of a block does not tell the count.

Cut the row into blocks of about `B = sqrt(n)` cells. Every block keeps the cells in a **sorted copy** and a **lazy addition** that applies to the whole block. A range operation touches at most two **partial** blocks and a run of **whole** blocks. For a whole block an addition only changes the lazy number, and a question is one binary search in the sorted copy for the threshold `x - lazy`. For a partial block, change or check the cells one by one and (after an addition) sort the block again.

body.code:
for b in range(bl + 1, br):                  # whole blocks
    kind 1: lz[b] += x
    kind 2: cnt += len(srt[b]) - bisect_left(srt[b], x - lz[b])
for i in partial parts:
    kind 1: val[i] += x      then   srt[block] = sorted(val[block])
    kind 2: cnt += (val[i] + lz[block] >= x)

body: The cost of an operation is O(B log B) for the partial blocks plus O((n / B) log B) for the whole ones, which is about O(sqrt(n) log n); with `n = q = 20000` that is a few thousand simple steps per operation. The values stay below `2 * 10^13`, so 64-bit integers are enough.

statement: A row of `n` numbers is given. Process `q` operations: type 1 `l r x` adds `x` to every number at the positions `l` to `r`; type 2 `l r x` asks how many numbers at the positions `l` to `r` are at least `x`. Print the answers to the questions on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of cells and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the cells.
Each of the next `q` lines has four numbers `t`, `l`, `r` and `x`. If `t = 1`, add `x` to every cell from `l` to `r`. If `t = 2`, print how many cells from `l` to `r` are at least `x`.
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.

examples.note: The numbers at least 3 in 3 1 4 1 5 are 3, 4 and 5. After adding 2 to the cells 2..4 the row is 3 3 6 3 5 and all 5 numbers are at least 3; among the cells 2..4 all 3 are: 3 5 3.

hints: Cut the row into blocks of about sqrt(n) cells.
Keep for every block a sorted copy of its cells and a lazy number added to all of them.
A whole block answers with one binary search for x minus its lazy number; a partial block is handled cell by cell and sorted again after a change.

explanation: The row is cut into blocks of about sqrt(n) cells. Each block keeps a sorted copy and a lazy addition; whole blocks are updated by the lazy number and queried by a binary search, partial blocks are handled cell by cell and sorted again after a change.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) sqrt(n) log n), space O(n).
